settings.privacy.noTelemetry: Envelope has no telemetry. Mail is stored only on this computer and your mail servers. AI features send only what you ask about to the provider you configure.

settings.shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
settings.shortcuts.label: Label
settings.advanced.signInClientsDesc: Google and Microsoft sign-in need an OAuth client registered for your installation. Official builds ship with one; if yours doesn't, register a free “Desktop app” client and paste its details here.
settings.about.desc: A fast, beautiful mail and calendar client for Linux. Free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license.
settings.encryption.desc: Envelope encrypts and signs mail with OpenPGP. It sends your public key along with your messages and picks up the keys of people who do the same (Autocrypt), so encryption is one click away whenever everyone in a conversation has a key.
settings.encryption.deleteOwnKeyConfirm: Messages encrypted to it can no longer be read unless you have a copy of the secret key elsewhere. Export it first if unsure.
settings.encryption.newKeyNote: A modern key (Ed25519 with a Curve25519 encryption key). It is stored in your system keyring.
settings.encryption.newKeyPassphraseHint: Asked once per session when set
settings.encryption.secretKeyField: Secret key (ASCII armored), or choose a file
settings.encryption.importPassphrase: Passphrase of the key (if it has one)
settings.encryption.exportWarning: Your secret key lets anyone read your encrypted mail and sign as you. Keep the file somewhere safe and never send it to anyone.
settings.encryption.exportPassphrase: Protect the file with a passphrase (recommended)
settings.encryption.otherOwnKeysDesc: Not used for sending, but still used to read mail encrypted to them.
settings.encryption.nowSendingFrom: Now sending from {email} with this key
settings.encryption.encryptWhenPossibleD: Turn on encryption automatically when every recipient has a key, and ask others to encrypt to you.
settings.encryption.signByDefaultDesc: Recipients can check that a message is from you. Encrypted messages are signed either way.
settings.encryption.sendAutocrypt: Send my public key with messages
settings.encryption.sendAutocryptDesc: An Autocrypt header lets other apps encrypt to you. Envelope creates a key for an address when it has none.
settings.encryption.protectSubjectDesc: The subject travels inside the encryption; servers and onlookers see “...”.
settings.encryption.wkdLookupDesc: While you write, ask the recipient's own mail domain (Web Key Directory) for a missing key. No other server is contacted.
settings.encryption.keepDecryptedDesc: Keep decrypted text on this device so encrypted mail can be searched and shows a preview. Off: it is decrypted each time you open it and only kept in memory.
settings.encryption.forgetDecryptedTitle: Forget the decrypted copies kept on this device?
settings.encryption.forgetDecryptedConfi: Encrypted messages stay readable; they are decrypted again when you open them.
settings.encryption.passphrasesDesc: Passphrases you enter are remembered until you quit Envelope.
settings.encryption.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, address or fingerprint
settings.encryption.publicKeysField: Public keys (ASCII armored), or choose a file
settings.encryption.findPlaceholder: Find a key by e-mail address
settings.encryption.findHint: Asks the address's domain and keys.openpgp.org
settings.encryption.verifyNote: Ask {name} to read out their fingerprint (in person, on a call, or through a channel you trust) and compare it with this one. If every group matches, messages from this key really come from them.
settings.encryption.noKeysYet: No keys yet. They arrive with mail from people who use encryption, or you can import or find them.
onboarding.welcomeLead: Mail and calendar that keep up with you. Fast, private and beautifully simple.
onboarding.featureInstantDesc: Everything is stored locally, so search and navigation never wait.
onboarding.featurePrivateDesc: Trackers and remote images are blocked. Your mail stays on your machine.
onboarding.featureSmartDesc: Optional AI with the provider you choose — summaries, replies, answers.
onboarding.addAccountSub: Choose your provider, or type your address and we'll figure out the rest.
onboarding.oauthIntro: Your browser will open to sign in securely. Envelope never sees your password — it receives a token that only allows access to mail, calendar and contacts.
onboarding.oauthNoClientGoogle: This build has no Google sign-in client configured. Add your own in {settings} or use an app password instead.
onboarding.oauthNoClientMicrosoft: This build has no Microsoft sign-in client configured. Add your own in {settings}.
onboarding.hintGoogleAppPassword: Use an app password from your Google Account (2-Step Verification required).
onboarding.hintIcloud: iCloud needs an app-specific password. Create one at account.apple.com → Sign-In and Security.
onboarding.hintYahoo: Yahoo needs an app password from Account security → App passwords.
onboarding.hintFastmail: Create an app password in Fastmail Settings → Privacy & Security.
onboarding.errorMissingCredentials: Enter your e-mail address and password.
onboarding.exchangeNote: Sign in with the password you use for Outlook or your work computer. Envelope finds your organization's Exchange server on its own; if it can't, enter the server under Advanced.
onboarding.serverHint: Leave empty to find it automatically. A server name or the full address ending in /EWS/Exchange.asmx both work.
onboarding.doneLead: {email} is syncing. Recent mail appears in seconds; older history keeps downloading in the background.
